<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
As an amusing sidenote, the other famous mathematical object named for August Ferdinand M\"{o}bius, the {\it M\"{o}bius strip}, is also a configuration space: $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Conf}}^{2}(S^{1})$.
<!-- end rem-1 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:phizetaformula}
As formal Dirichlet series, 
$$
\sum_{n = 1}^{\infty} \frac{\phi(n)}{n^{s}} = \frac{\zeta_{\mathbb{Q}}(s - 1)}{\zeta_{\mathbb{Q}}(s)}. 
$$
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By Dirichlet convolution, 
$$
\sum_{n = 1}^{\infty} \frac{\phi(n)}{n^{s}} = \left (\sum_{n = 1}^{\infty} \frac{n}{n^{s}}\right )\left (\sum_{n = 1}^{\infty} \frac{\mu(n)}{n^{s}}\right ) = \zeta_{\mathbb{Q}}(s - 1)\mu_{\mathbb{Q}}(s) = \zeta_{\mathbb{Q}}(s - 1)\zeta_{\mathbb{Q}}(s)^{-1}. 
$$
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- defn-1: body_md -->
The {\bf totient function of a number field} $K/\mathbb{Q}$ is the function $\phi_{K} : I_{K}^{+}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}$ defined by 
$$
\phi_{K}(\frak{a}) = \#(\mathcal{O}_{K}/\frak{a})^{\times}. 
$$
<!-- end defn-1 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
For any ideal $\frak{a}\in I_{K}^{+}$, 
\begin{equation}
N(\frak{a}) = \sum_{\frak{d}\mid\frak{a}} \phi_{K}(\frak{d})
\end{equation}
where the sum runs over all ideals $\frak{d}$ dividing $\frak{a}$. In other words, $N = \phi_{K}*\zeta$ where $\zeta(\frak{a}) = 1$ is the zeta function for $I_{K}^{+}$.
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
By formula (\ref{eq:Dedekindtotientprod}), 
$$
\phi_{K}(\frak{a}) = N(\frak{a})\prod_{\frak{p}\mid\frak{a}} \left (1 - \frac{1}{N(\frak{p})}\right ) = N(\frak{a})\sum_{\frak{d}\mid\frak{a}} \frac{\mu(\frak{d})}{N(\frak{d})} = \sum_{\frak{d}\mid\frak{a}} \mu(\frak{d})N(\frak{ad}^{-1}). 
$$
This can be rewritten 
\begin{equation}
\phi_{K}(\frak{a}) = \sum_{\frak{d}\mid\frak{a}} N(\frak{d})\mu(\frak{ad}^{-1})
\end{equation}
i.e.~$\phi_{K} = N*\mu$. Then M\"{o}bius inversion gives the desired formula.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- rem-2: body_md -->
We could have proved formula (\ref{eq:totientrecur}) for the classical totient function this way too, i.e.~by first proving formula (\ref{eq:classicalmobius}) directly using the above argument and then applying M\"{o}bius inversion.
<!-- end rem-2 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:Dedekindphizetaformula}
As formal Dirichlet series, 
\begin{equation}
\sum_{\frak{a}\in I_{K}^{+}} \frac{\phi_{K}(\frak{a})}{N(\frak{a})^{s}} = \frac{\zeta_{K}(s - 1)}{\zeta_{K}(s)}. 
\end{equation}
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Since $\phi_{K} = N*\mu$, we get 
$$
\sum_{\frak{a}\in I_{K}^{+}} \frac{\phi_{K}(\frak{a})}{N(\frak{a})^{s}} = \left (\sum_{\frak{a}\in I_{K}^{+}} \frac{N(\frak{a})}{N(\frak{a})^{s}}\right )\left (\sum_{\frak{a}\in I_{K}^{+}} \frac{\mu(\frak{a})}{N(\frak{a})^{s}}\right ) = \zeta_{K}(s - 1)\mu_{K}(s) = \zeta_{K}(s - 1)\zeta_{K}(s)^{-1}. 
$$
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- defn-2: body_md -->
The {\bf totient function of a variety} $X/\mathbb{F}_{q}$ is the function $\phi_{X} : Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}$ defined by 
$$
\phi_{X}(\alpha) = \#(\mathcal{O}_{X,\alpha}/I_{\alpha})^{\times}. 
$$
<!-- end defn-2 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
For any effective $0$-cycle $\alpha$ on $X$, 
\begin{equation}
q^{\deg(\alpha)} = \sum_{\beta\leq\alpha} \phi_{X}(\beta). 
\end{equation}
In other words, $\pi = \phi_{X}*\zeta$, where $\zeta(\alpha) = 1$ is the zeta function for $Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)$ and $\pi = q^{\deg(-)}$.
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Write $\alpha = \sum_{i = 1}^{r} a_{i}x_{i}$. By formula (\ref{eq:HWtotientprod}), 
$$
\phi_{X}(\alpha) = q^{\deg(\alpha)}\prod_{i = 1}^{r} (1 - q^{-\deg(x_{i})}) = q^{\deg(\alpha)}\sum_{\beta\leq\alpha} \mu(\beta)q^{-\deg(\beta)} = \sum_{\beta\leq\alpha} \mu(\beta)q^{\deg(\alpha - \beta)}
$$
where $\mu$ is the M\"{o}bius function for $Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)$. This can be rewritten 
\begin{equation}
\phi_{X}(\alpha) = \sum_{\beta\leq\alpha} \mu(\beta)q^{\deg(\alpha - \beta)} = \sum_{\beta\leq\alpha} q^{\deg(\beta)}\mu(\alpha - \beta). 
\end{equation}
Or in other words, $\phi_{X} = \pi*\mu$. Then M\"{o}bius inversion for $Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)$ implies that $\pi = \phi_{X}*\zeta$ as claimed.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:HWphizetaformula}
For any variety $X$ over a finite field, 
$$
\sum_{\alpha\in Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)} \phi_{X}(\alpha)t^{\deg(\alpha)} = \frac{Z(X\times\mathbb{A}^{1},t)}{Z(X,t)}. 
$$
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Translating the identity $\phi_{X} = \pi*\mu$ to power series produces 
\begin{align*}
  \sum_{\alpha\in Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)} \phi_{X}(\alpha)t^{\deg(\alpha)} &= \left (\sum_{\alpha\in Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)} q^{\deg(\alpha)}t^{\deg(\alpha)}\right )\left (\sum_{\alpha\in Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)} \mu(\alpha)t^{\deg(\alpha)}\right )\\
    &= \left (\sum_{\alpha\in Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)} (qt)^{\deg(\alpha)}\right )Z(X,t)^{-1} = Z(X,qt)Z(X,t)^{-1}.
\end{align*}
It is well-known that $Z(X,qt) = Z(X\times\mathbb{A}^{1},t)$, so the claimed formula holds.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- rem-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:totientmotivic}
Thinking motivically, we can see formula (\ref{eq:arithphizeta}) and its various special cases (Propositions~\ref{prop:phizetaformula}, \ref{prop:Dedekindphizetaformula} and~\ref{prop:HWphizetaformula}) as shadows of the identity $[\mathbb{A}^{1}] = [\mathbb{G}_{m}] + [\text{point}]$ in the Grothendieck ring of $\mathbb{Z}$-schemes (resp.~$\mathcal{O}_{K}$-schemes, $\mathbb{F}_{q}$-varieties).
<!-- end rem-3 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:eulernumberfield}
Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_{K}$. For any $\alpha\in\mathcal{O}_{K}$ and ideal $\frak{b}$ such that $\alpha\mathcal{O}_{K}$ and $\frak{b}$ are relatively prime, 
$$
\alpha^{\phi_{K}(\frak{b})} \equiv 1\pmod{\frak{b}}. 
$$
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- prop-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:eulervariety}
Let $X/\mathbb{F}_{q}$ be a variety, $U\subseteq X$ an open subset and $f\in\mathcal{O}_{X}(U)$. Then for any effective $0$-cycle $\beta\in Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)$ with support outside $V(f) = \{x\in U\mid f(x) = 0\}$, 
$$
f^{\phi_{X}(\beta)} \equiv 1\pmod{I_{\beta}}
$$
in the semilocal ring $\mathcal{O}_{X,\beta}$.
<!-- end prop-7 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
Let $k$ be a finite field, $g\in k[t]$ and $D = \ensuremath{\operatorname{div}}_{0}(g)$ the effective divisor of zeroes of $g$. Then 
\begin{enumerate}[\quad (1)]
    \item $\phi_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(D) = \#\{f\in k[t]\mid \deg(f) < \deg(g) \text{ and } \gcd(f,g) = 1\}$. 
    \item For any such $f\in k[t]$, 
    $$
    f^{\phi_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(D)} \equiv 1\pmod{g}
    $$
    holds in $k[t]$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Both statements follow from setting $X = \mathbb{P}^{1}$, $U = \mathbb{P}^{1}\smallsetminus\{\infty\} \cong \mathbb{A}^{1}$, identifying the rings $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1},D} \cong k[t]/(g)$ and taking cardinalities of multiplicative groups of units.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- defn-3: body_md -->
The {\bf first divisor sum of a number field} $K/\mathbb{Q}$ is the arithmetic function $\sigma_{1,K} : I_{K}^{\times}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}$ defined by 
$$
\sigma_{1,K}(\frak{a}) = \#\mathbb{P}^{1}(\mathcal{O}_{K}/\frak{a}). 
$$
<!-- end defn-3 -->
<!-- prop-8: body_md -->
As formal Dirichlet series, 
$$
\sum_{\frak{a}\in I_{K}^{+}} \frac{\sigma_{1,K}(\frak{a})}{N(\frak{a})^{s}} = \zeta_{K}(s)\zeta_{K}(s - 1). 
$$
<!-- end prop-8 -->
<!-- defn-4: body_md -->
The {\bf first divisor sum of a variety} $X/\mathbb{F}_{q}$ is the function $\sigma_{1,X} : Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}$ defined by 
$$
\sigma_{1,X}(\alpha) = \#\mathbb{P}^{1}(\mathcal{O}_{X,\alpha}/I_{\alpha}). 
$$
<!-- end defn-4 -->
<!-- prop-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:sigma1variety}
For any variety $X/\mathbb{F}_{q}$, 
$$
\sum_{\alpha\in Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)} \sigma_{1,K}(\alpha)t^{\deg(\alpha)} = Z(X,t)Z(X\times\mathbb{A}^{1},t). 
$$
<!-- end prop-9 -->
<!-- defn-5: body_md -->
For an arithmetic scheme $X$, the {\bf global first divisor sum} of $X$ is the formal power series 
$$
S_{1,X}(s) = \prod_{p\text{ prime}} S_{1}(X_{p},p^{-s})
$$
where for each prime $p$, 
$$
S_{1}(X_{p},t) = \sum_{\alpha\in Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X_{p})} \sigma_{1,X_{p}}(\alpha)t^{\deg(\alpha)}. 
$$
<!-- end defn-5 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
For any arithmetic scheme $X$, we have 
$$
S_{1,X}(s) = \zeta_{X}(s)\zeta_{X}(s - 1). 
$$
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- rem-4: body_md -->
\label{rem:sigmamotivic}
As in Remark~\ref{rem:totientmotivic}, we can view the formulas above as shadows of the formula $[\mathbb{P}^{1}] = [\mathbb{A}^{1}] + [\text{point}]$ in the appropriate Grothendieck ring. Further, formula (\ref{eq:divisorsumDirichletseries}) also suggests generalizing the divisor sum functions $\sigma_{m}(n)$ by $\sigma_{m,X}(z) = \#(\mathcal{O}/z)^{m} + 1$ for each choice of object $X$, ring $\mathcal{O}$ and monoid $Z$ with $z\in Z$. That is, a divisor sum function is a shadow of a class of the form $[\mathbb{A}^{m}] + [\text{point}]$ in some Grothendieck ring.
<!-- end rem-4 -->
<!-- defn-6: body_md -->
{\bf Dedekind's $\psi$-function} is the arithmetic function $\psi : \mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ defined by 
$$
\psi(n) = n\prod_{p\mid n} \left (1 + \frac{1}{p}\right ). 
$$
<!-- end defn-6 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
$\#G(p^{k}) = \psi(p^{k})$.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
This follows from standard formulas for $\#\mathbb{W}_{k}(\mathbb{F}_{q})$ and $\#\mathbb{W}_{k}(\mathbb{F}_{q})^{\times}$. For more details, see \cite{kzb}.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
$\#G(n) = \psi(n)$.
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- question-1: body_md -->
\label{q:bigwitt}
Is there a group scheme $\mathcal{G}/\ensuremath{\operatorname{Spec}}\mathbb{Z}$ such that $G(n) \cong \mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})$ for all $n$? For example, is there an interpretation of the groups $G(n)$ in terms of the ring of big Witt vectors?
<!-- end question-1 -->
<!-- defn-7: body_md -->
The {\bf $\psi$-function of a number field} $K/\mathbb{Q}$ is the function $\psi_{K} : I_{K}^{\times}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}$ defined by 
$$
\psi_{K}(\frak{a}) = N(\frak{a})\prod_{\frak{p}\mid\frak{a}} \left (1 + \frac{1}{N(\frak{p})}\right ). 
$$
<!-- end defn-7 -->
<!-- prop-10: body_md -->
\label{prop:numberfieldpsiprops}
Let $\frak{a},\frak{b},\frak{p}\subset\mathcal{O}_{K}$ be ideals, with $\frak{p}$ prime. Then 
\begin{enumerate}[\quad (a)]
    \item If $\frak{a}$ and $\frak{b}$ are relatively prime, then $\psi_{K}(\frak{a}\frak{b}) = \psi_{K}(\frak{a})\psi_{K}(\frak{b})$. 
    \item $\psi_{K}(\frak{p}) = \sigma_{1,K}(\frak{p}) = N(\frak{p}) + 1$. In particular, if $\frak{a}$ is squarefree then $\psi_{K}(\frak{a}) = \sigma_{1,K}(\frak{a})$. 
    \item As arithmetic functions on $I_{K}^{\times}$, $\psi_{K} = N*|\mu_{K}|$, where $\mu_{K}$ is the M\"{o}bius function in $I(I_{K}^{\times})$. 
    \item $\psi(\frak{a}) = [SL_{2}(\mathcal{O}_{K}) : \Gamma_{0}(\frak{a})]$, where $\Gamma_{0}(\frak{a})$ is the subgroup of matrices in $SL_{2}(\mathcal{O}_{K})$ which are upper triangular mod $\frak{a}$. 
    \item $\psi_{K}(\frak{a}) = \#G(\frak{a})$ where 
    $$
    G(\frak{a}) := \prod_{\frak{p}^{k}\mid\mid\frak{a}} G(\frak{p}^{k}) := \prod_{\frak{p}^{k}\mid\mid\frak{a}} \mathbb{W}_{k}(\mathbb{F}_{N(\frak{p})^{2}})^{\times}/\mathbb{W}_{k}(\mathbb{F}_{N(\frak{p})})^{\times}. 
    $$
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-10 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
(a) -- (c) follow from the definition. (d) is proven in the usual way, i.e.~by counting the number of cyclic submodules of rank $N(\frak{a})$ in $E[\frak{a}]$, where $E$ is an elliptic curve over $K$ (equivalently, cyclic submodules in $E_{tors}$ which are isomorphic as $\mathcal{O}_{K}$-modules to $\mathcal{O}_{K}/\frak{a}$). Finally, (e) follows from the same standard formulas as above.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- cor-4: body_md -->
The Dirichlet series for $\psi_{K}$ satisfies the formula 
$$
\sum_{\frak{a}\subset\mathcal{O}_{K}} \frac{\psi_{K}(\frak{a})}{N(\frak{a})^{s}} = \frac{\zeta_{K}(s)\zeta_{K}(s - 1)}{\zeta_{K}(2s)}
$$
where $\zeta_{K}(s)$ is the Dedekind zeta function of $K$.
<!-- end cor-4 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
This follows from (c) and the identity 
$$
\sum_{\frak{a}\subset\mathcal{O}_{K}} \frac{|\mu_{K}(\frak{a})|}{N(\frak{a})^{s}} = \frac{\zeta_{K}(s)}{\zeta_{K}(2s)}
$$
which is a straightforward generalization of the same formula over $\mathbb{Q}$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- defn-8: body_md -->
The {\bf $\psi$-function of a variety} $X/\mathbb{F}_{q}$ is the function $\psi_{X} : Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}$ defined by 
$$
\psi_{X}(\alpha) = q^{\deg(\alpha)}\prod_{i = 1}^{r} (1 + q^{-\deg(x_{i})}). 
$$
<!-- end defn-8 -->
<!-- prop-11: body_md -->
Let $\alpha,\beta\in Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)$ and let $x\in|X|$. Then 
\begin{enumerate}[\quad (a)]
    \item If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are relatively prime, then $\psi_{X}(\alpha + \beta) = \psi_{X}(\alpha)\psi_{X}(\beta)$. 
    \item $\psi_{X}(x) = \sigma_{1,X}(x) = q^{\deg(x)} + 1$. In particular, if $\alpha$ is a {\it log} effective $0$-cycle\footnote{A log cycle is one for which each irreducible cycle appears with coefficient $1$.} then $\psi_{X}(\alpha) = \sigma_{1,X}(\alpha)$. 
    \item As arithmetic functions on $Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)$, $\psi_{X} = \pi*|\mu_{X}|$, where $\mu_{X}$ is the M\"{o}bius function in $I(Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X))$. 
    \item $\psi(\alpha) = [SL_{2}(\mathcal{O}_{X,\alpha}) : \Gamma_{0}(I_{\alpha})]$, where $\Gamma_{0}(I_{\alpha})$ is the subgroup of matrices in $SL_{2}(\mathcal{O}_{X,\alpha})$ which are upper triangular mod $I_{\alpha}$. 
    \item $\psi_{X}(\alpha) = \#G(\alpha)$ where 
    $$
    G(\alpha) := \prod_{kx\in\alpha} G(kx) := \prod_{kx\in\alpha} \mathbb{W}_{k}(\mathbb{F}_{q^{2\deg(\alpha)}})^{\times}/\mathbb{W}_{k}(\mathbb{F}_{q^{\deg(\alpha)}})^{\times}. 
    $$
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-11 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
(a) -- (c) and (e) are the same as in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:numberfieldpsiprops}. For (e), counting sublattices in $(\mathcal{O}_{X,\alpha}/I_{\alpha})^{2}$ isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}_{X,\alpha}/I_{\alpha}$ gives the result.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- cor-5: body_md -->
The power series for $\psi_{X}$ satisfies 
$$
\sum_{\alpha\in Z_{0}^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{eff}}}(X)} \psi_{X}(\alpha)t^{\deg(\alpha)} = \frac{Z(X,t)Z(X,qt)}{Z(X,t^{2})} = \frac{Z(X,t)Z(X\times\mathbb{A}^{1},t)}{Z(X_{\mathbb{F}_{q^{2}}},t)}
$$
where $X_{\mathbb{F}_{q^{2}}} = X\times_{\ensuremath{\operatorname{Spec}}\mathbb{F}_{q}}\ensuremath{\operatorname{Spec}}\mathbb{F}_{q^{2}}$.
<!-- end cor-5 -->
<!-- cor-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:globalpsi}
For any arithmetic scheme $X$, we have 
$$
\Psi_{X}(s) = \frac{\zeta_{X}(s)\zeta_{X\times\mathbb{A}^{1}}(s)}{\zeta_{X}(2s)}. 
$$
<!-- end cor-6 -->
<!-- defn-9: body_md -->
{\bf Liouville's $\lambda$-function} is the arithmetic function $\lambda : \mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ defined by $\lambda(1) = 1$ and 
$$
\lambda(n) = \begin{cases}
  1, &\text{if $n$ is a product of an even number of primes}\\
  -1, &\text{if $n$ is a product of an odd number of primes}. 
\end{cases}
$$
That is, $\lambda(n) = (-1)^{\Omega(n)}$ where $\Omega\left (\prod p_{i}^{a_{i}}\right ) = \sum a_{i}$.
<!-- end defn-9 -->
<!-- problem-1: body_md -->
\label{prob:lambda}
Extend $\lambda$ to a number field $K/\mathbb{Q}$ by setting 
$$
\lambda_{K}(\frak{a}) = (-1)^{\Omega(\frak{a})}
$$
where $\Omega\left (\prod \frak{p}_{i}^{a_{i}}\right ) = \sum a_{i}$. Show $\lambda_{K}*|\mu_{K}| = \delta$ in the incidence algebra $I(I_{K}^{\times})$, which implies 
$$
\sum_{\frak{a}\subset\mathcal{O}_{K}} \frac{\lambda_{K}(\frak{a})}{N(\frak{a})^{s}} = \frac{\zeta_{K}(2s)}{\zeta_{K}(s)}. 
$$
Repeat for a variety $X/\mathbb{F}_{q}$ and for a scheme $X/\ensuremath{\operatorname{Spec}}\mathbb{Z}$.
<!-- end problem-1 -->
<!-- problem-2: body_md -->
If possible, find a class $\xi$ in the Grothendieck ring of schemes such that $\#\xi(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}) = \lambda(n)$ and similarly for each generalization of $\psi$ in Problem~\ref{prob:lambda}.
<!-- end problem-2 -->
<!-- question-2: body_md -->
Does this identity generalize to (i) number fields? (ii) higher dimensional geometric objects? (iii) a formula in some Grothendieck ring? What about formulas involving the sum of squares functions $r_{k}(n)$ for $k\geq 3$?
<!-- end question-2 -->
